D019-D020_h001.question: "I've been feeling so unlike myself since my husband passed away three weeks ago. It's like a bad dream I can't wake up from. Every night, I just toss and turn. I can get a full eight hours, sometimes more, but I wake up feeling just as tired as when I went to bed, like I haven't slept at all. The worst part is these flashes I get. I'll be in the middle of cleaning, and suddenly, I'm right back in the hospital room, seeing him, hearing the doctor. It’s like it’s happening all over again, and I lose track of where I am for a few moments. It's been like this pretty much since... well, since that day. It's hard to focus on anything, even my housework, with these things popping up."
D019-D020_h001.options:
A. Adjustment Disorder
    B. Posttraumatic Stress Disorder
    C. Acute Stress Disorder
    D. Attention-Deficit/Hyperactivity Disorder (Combined Presentation)

D019-D020_h002.question: It's been a rough couple of months, doctor. Ever since the accident with the pedestrian, I just haven't been myself. That happened about five weeks ago now. I keep waking up in the middle of the night, feeling absolutely panicked, and then it's a battle to get back to sleep. And when I do manage to drift off, it's those dreams. Always about the accident, reliving it over and over, that same sickening crunch. It’s hard to focus during the day, making every fare feel like an uphill climb. I’m just so on edge all the time. My ex-wife says I’m isolating myself, and she’s probably right, but I just don’t have the energy to pretend everything’s fine. It feels like this started right after a big fight I had with my ex-wife and a lot of money issues with my taxi company. I know it's a lot, and I haven't really been able to cope.
D019-D020_h002.options:
A. Adjustment Disorder
    B. Posttraumatic Stress Disorder
    C. Acute Stress Disorder
    D. Attention-Deficit/Hyperactivity Disorder (Combined Presentation)

D019-D020_h003.question: "My husband kept telling me I should come in, and honestly, I haven't been myself since... well, since that story broke last month. It was about the embezzlement at the city council, a really big expose, and it just spiraled. I'm usually so good at compartmentalizing work, but this one stuck. Even though it's been a few weeks, I still feel on edge. I'm so tired, even after a full eight hours of sleep, I wake up feeling like I haven't rested at all. And if I see anything in the news related to financial crime, or even just hear a siren, my stomach drops, and I get this horrible knot of anxiety. It’s been about three weeks since the initial rush of the story, and while I’m not reliving anything like a nightmare or flashback, the general feeling of dread is constant. It’s hard to focus on new assignments, and even at home, I just feel...off."
D019-D020_h003.options:
A. Adjustment Disorder
    B. Posttraumatic Stress Disorder
    C. Acute Stress Disorder
    D. Attention-Deficit/Hyperactivity Disorder (Combined Presentation)

D019-D020_h004.question:
It’s all just... a lot. It started maybe a month and a half ago, right after that really tough week on call where we lost Mrs. Henderson. I just can't shake it.

Every night, I dread going to bed. My mind just races, replaying everything. It takes me forever to actually fall asleep, sometimes hours. And during the day, even just seeing a patient who reminds me of her, or hearing an ambulance siren, sends my stomach into knots. I get this wave of intense distress; it’s like I’m right back in that ICU room. I know it’s impacting my focus at work, and my attendings have noticed. I'm worried about making a mistake. I just feel constantly on edge and overwhelmed. The strange thing is, even though it's been about six weeks since that incident, I don't feel like I'm having flashbacks or anything like that, and I can still function, albeit poorly. But this feeling of dread and sleeplessness... it's just constant.
D019-D020_h004.options:
A. Adjustment Disorder
    B. Posttraumatic Stress Disorder
    C. Acute Stress Disorder
    D. Attention-Deficit/Hyperactivity Disorder (Combined Presentation)

D019-D020_h005.question: It’s been a rough patch since my wife passed, about six weeks ago now. Being a night watchman, solitude is part of the job, but now it feels… different. I used to manage fine, but lately, I’m just a shell. I only get a few hours of sleep, maybe from 1 to 4 AM if I'm lucky, and then I’m wide awake, staring at the ceiling. Everywhere I look, there's something that reminds me of her – a piece of her clothing, a photo, even the old armchair. It just sends this pang through my chest, makes it hard to breathe. It’s not like those panic attacks some people describe, but it’s a deep, deep sadness that washes over me, relentless. The doctor suggested I come here because these feelings, this distress, it’s not letting up.
D019-D020_h005.options:
A. Adjustment Disorder
    B. Posttraumatic Stress Disorder
    C. Acute Stress Disorder
    D. Attention-Deficit/Hyperactivity Disorder (Combined Presentation)

D019-D020_h006.question:
It’s been a tough few weeks, Doc, ever since the near-miss incident mid-flight last month. I can’t seem to get a proper night’s rest. I wake up around 3 AM, sometimes 4, and that's it—my mind just starts racing. Even if I try to go back to sleep, it just won’t happen.

I keep replaying bits of that day, but it’s strange. I can vividly remember the turbulence and the sudden drop, the feeling in my gut, but then other parts, like what I said to air traffic control right after, or the exact sequence of events in the cockpit during the worst of it, are just… fuzzy. It's like a bad dream where you only remember fragments. It's been a month now since it happened, so I know I don't have acute stress disorder.

Even with my daughter's graduation last week, which I should have been thrilled about, I just felt flat. My wife threw me a surprise party for my 50th, and I couldn't crack a genuine smile. It’s like the capacity for happiness just… isn't there anymore.
D019-D020_h006.options:
A. Posttraumatic Stress Disorder
    B. Acute Stress Disorder
    C. Adjustment Disorder
    D. Bulimia Nervosa

D019-D020_h007.question: "My editor, Sarah, she abruptly left the paper about two months ago. It was a complete shock. We were working on this huge investigative piece together, and then... nothing. I guess I’ve been struggling ever since. It's been impacting everything. I'm just so on edge all the time since she left. I don't feel like myself. I'm usually so driven, but now, even when I land a great interview or get a positive response to a draft, I just feel… flat. There's no sense of accomplishment. And the sleep? Forget it. Every night I have these vivid, terrifying dreams, always about the article falling apart or Sarah just disappearing mid-sentence. It makes me dread going to bed. Honestly, sometimes I can barely remember the details of the weeks leading up to her leaving, almost like my brain has blocked it out. It's not like I'm having flashbacks or anything, I just feel this persistent anhedonia and heightened anxiety. It’s been about eight weeks now since she left, and these feelings really started not long after, within the first few weeks."
D019-D020_h007.options:
A. Posttraumatic Stress Disorder
    B. Acute Stress Disorder
    C. Adjustment Disorder
    D. Bulimia Nervosa

D019-D020_h008.question: It’s been a crazy few weeks. About three weeks ago, my team just totally flamed out during the regional qualifiers – the biggest match of my life, you know? Since then, my head’s been a mess. I keep having these really vivid nightmares, always about making that final, horrible mistake in the game; they really mess with my sleep. During the day, it's weird, I can remember bits and pieces of the actual game – like specific plays or what my teammates were yelling – but the really crucial moments, the big turning points where we messed up? It’s like my mind just blacks out those parts. I feel so hollow, like I can't even get excited about anything anymore, not even playing other games, which used to be my whole life. I’ve just been going through the motions, feeling nothing. I know it’s only been three weeks, but it feels like hitting a wall.
D019-D020_h008.options:
A. Posttraumatic Stress Disorder
    B. Acute Stress Disorder
    C. Adjustment Disorder
    D. Bulimia Nervosa

D019-D020_h009.question: "Lately, I've just been… off. It started a little over a month ago, right after that incident at the cafe. I was robbed at knifepoint, and even though no one was hurt, it really messed me up. I’ve been sleeping so much, like, seriously long stretches at night, and then I’m still dragging myself through the day, desperate for a nap. It’s weird, I can remember the guy being there, the knife, the fear, but then there are parts in between, like what I exactly said or did, that are just blank. And even though my manager has been really understanding and even gave me a bonus for handling it well, I just can't feel good about anything. It’s like, what’s there to be proud of? I just feel this persistent low mood. I know it’s been a bit over a month, and the immediate panic has smoothed out, but I'm still not myself."
D019-D020_h009.options:
A. Posttraumatic Stress Disorder
    B. Acute Stress Disorder
    C. Adjustment Disorder
    D. Bulimia Nervosa

D019-D020_h010.question:
"Doc, I’m just… not myself. It’s been a few weeks since that accident on the rig, maybe a month now. I keep waking up at 3 AM, every single night, and that's it—my mind starts racing, and sleep's just gone. It's not like I can even fully remember what happened, actually. Most of that day is a blur; chunks of it are completely missing, like my brain just wiped it.

The oddest part is how I feel about my folks. My mom came to visit, and while I know I love her, I just felt… nothing. It’s like the capacity to feel that sort of warmth, that love, has just shut down inside me. It's not that I'm seeing things or having flashbacks; none of that has happened. I just feel incredibly hollow, and it’s getting harder to just go through the motions."
D019-D020_h010.options:
A. Posttraumatic Stress Disorder
    B. Acute Stress Disorder
    C. Adjustment Disorder
    D. Bulimia Nervosa

D019-D020_h011.question:
It’s been a rough few months. My husband and I went through a really tough time with his health scare back in March – thankfully he’s doing better now, but I just can’t seem to get back to normal. It’s like my brain is stuck. Every morning, I stare at my closet for ages, completely unable to decide what to wear for appointments. Even picking what to have for dinner feels like a monumental task now.

I’m constantly on edge, especially when I’m showing houses. I find myself always scanning the room, making sure I know where every exit is and who’s around me. It feels a bit silly, but I can't help it. And if someone unexpectedly brushes against me, even accidentally, I practically jump out of my skin. It's just so frustrating because this all started right after things began to calm down with my husband’s health, and it's been going on for a solid month now. I know it’s not what people usually think of as ‘trauma,’ but it felt traumatic to me, and these feelings haven't let up.
D019-D020_h011.options:
A. Posttraumatic Stress Disorder
    B. Schizophrenia
    C. Adjustment Disorder
    D. Acute Stress Disorder

D019-D020_h012.question: It's been... I'd say about four months now since the last major incident on that transatlantic flight. Ever since then, things just aren't right. I'm finding it nearly impossible to make any decisions, even simple ones. My wife asks me what I want for dinner and I just freeze. My mind goes blank. Getting dressed in the morning feels like a monumental task. I’m just constantly on edge, like I’m still in the cockpit scanning instruments, even when I'm just sitting at home. Every little sudden sound, a car horn, an unexpected door closing, it makes me jump out of my skin. It's been like this for a while, definitely started a few weeks after that flight, but it hasn't been a full blown crisis situation, thankfully.
D019-D020_h012.options:
A. Posttraumatic Stress Disorder
    B. Schizophrenia
    C. Adjustment Disorder
    D. Acute Stress Disorder

D019-D020_h013.question: "It's just been a lot since the divorce finalized a little over a month ago. I feel like my mind is constantly wrapped in a fog; it’s hard to think straight, to focus on anything beyond basic tasks at work. I keep catching myself looking around constantly, like I’m waiting for something bad to happen, even when I’m just walking down the grocery aisle. The other day, a colleague just came up to my desk to ask a question and I literally jumped out of my skin – like I was genuinely startled. It’s been three weeks since the divorce, and these feelings have been pretty intense, but they don't quite feel like everything I've read about acute stress disorder."
D019-D020_h013.options:
A. Posttraumatic Stress Disorder
    B. Schizophrenia
    C. Adjustment Disorder
    D. Acute Stress Disorder

D019-D020_h014.question: "It all started about three weeks ago, right after that awful restructuring at work. I know it's HR, but seeing so many colleagues let go, it just hit me hard. Before that, I was fine. Now, my mind just feels… foggy. It’s like there’s a veil over everything, making it impossible to focus on anything important. I find myself constantly checking the exits whenever I'm in a new meeting room, or even just looking around the cafeteria, trying to make sure everything feels safe. And if someone taps me on the shoulder unexpectedly? I jump out of my skin every single time, my heart just pounds. It’s not like those big, intense flashbacks or a complete emotional numbness, but I just don't feel like myself, and it all definitely began after the restructuring, not even a month ago."
D019-D020_h014.options:
A. Posttraumatic Stress Disorder
    B. Schizophrenia
    C. Adjustment Disorder
    D. Acute Stress Disorder

D019-D020_h015.question: "I've just been feeling... off, for a few weeks now. It all started after that car accident I witnessed last month. It wasn't me, but I was right there. I don't know, it shook me up more than I thought it would. My mind feels cloudy, like there's a fog in my head, especially when I'm trying to focus on designs at work. It’s hard to concentrate. I’m constantly looking over my shoulder, checking the exits in coffee shops, watching people's hands when they walk by. And every little noise makes me jump. A door slamming, a dropped pen, I flinch and my heart absolutely races. It’s been happening for about three weeks now, since roughly a week after the accident. I know it’s not full-blown PTSD or anything like that, but I'm really struggling."
D019-D020_h015.options:
A. Posttraumatic Stress Disorder
    B. Schizophrenia
    C. Adjustment Disorder
    D. Acute Stress Disorder

D019-D020_h016.question:
It’s been a rough few weeks, honestly. Everything just feels… off. I’m thinking back to that night in the ER when we had that massive pile-up – bodies everywhere, blood, the screams… I keep seeing flashes of it, especially when I’m trying to relax at home. It’s like a movie playing on a loop in my head, whether I want it to or not.

I've also been actively avoiding the break room because a lot of the talk there is about what happened, and I just can't. Even the news, I've completely cut myself off from; I change the channel if I hear anything that might trigger a memory. The weirdest part, though, is I can’t clearly recall the whole event, just bits and pieces. It’s like certain parts are just… gone. This all started about a month ago, a few days after that shift, but it's not like the absolute panic or disconnect some of my colleagues described right after. It's more of a lingering shadow.
D019-D020_h016.options:
A. Acute Stress Disorder
    B. Adjustment Disorder
    C. Posttraumatic Stress Disorder
    D. Schizoaffective Disorder (Bipolar Type)

D019-D020_h017.question: I just haven't been myself since the fire at the shop last month. It started with a faulty wire, and even though nobody was hurt, seeing everything I've built up over the years go up in smoke... it still feels unreal. For a good while after, I just couldn’t think about it, couldn’t even fully remember the chaos of that day, almost like a blank spot in my memory for the worst parts. When I walk by the burnt-out building now, or even just catch a whiff of smoke from a neighbor’s chimney, my heart starts racing, and I get this overwhelming feeling of dread, like it’s happening all over again. I try to avoid that side of town completely now, and I definitely change the channel if anything about fires comes on TV. It's been about three weeks now, and while those intense initial reactions were really strong right after, it never quite escalated to *that* level I hear about on the news, where people are completely frozen or having those vivid flashbacks all the time. It’s more of a gnawing feeling, you know?
D019-D020_h017.options:
A. Acute Stress Disorder
    B. Adjustment Disorder
    C. Posttraumatic Stress Disorder
    D. Schizoaffective Disorder (Bipolar Type)

D019-D020_h018.question: It’s been almost two and a half months since that awful car accident, and honestly, I just don’t feel like myself. I know it wasn't a huge, earth-shattering event, but it really rattled me. I keep having these dreams, not about the accident itself, but they're always unsettling, tense. I wake up in a cold sweat, feeling the same anxiety I felt right after it happened. I try not to think about the accident at all. If a friend brings it up, I quickly change the subject, or I find myself getting up and leaving the room. It's like I can't even remember the full sequence of events, just bits and pieces, but the feelings are all there. It's difficult to focus on my writing, and I feel this constant knot in my stomach. Things felt off a couple of weeks after it happened; I just can't shake this feeling of dread.
D019-D020_h018.options:
A. Acute Stress Disorder
    B. Adjustment Disorder
    C. Posttraumatic Stress Disorder
    D. Schizoaffective Disorder (Bipolar Type)

D019-D020_h019.question: It’s been pretty rough lately, doctor. That kitchen fire last month really shook me up. I still see flashes of the flames, especially when I'm reaching for something on a high shelf or if I smell anything burning – my heart just starts pounding. I try really hard not to think about that night, to push away the images and feelings, but they sneak up on me, especially when I’m trying to relax at home. My wife, she’ll try to talk about it, but I just… I can’t. The weirdest thing is, I can't even remember how I got out of the restaurant. There’s a big chunk of that night that’s just gone. This all started happening right after the fire, maybe a week or so later, but I don't feel like it's taken over my life in the way I hear others describe after something really awful happens.
D019-D020_h019.options:
A. Acute Stress Disorder
    B. Adjustment Disorder
    C. Posttraumatic Stress Disorder
    D. Schizoaffective Disorder (Bipolar Type)

D019-D020_h020.question: It’s been a tough few weeks, Doc, ever since that robbery at the mall. I keep seeing it in my head—the guy with the gun, the fear in people’s eyes. It just pops up, unbidden, even when I'm trying to relax with my wife. I've been trying to push those images away, those thoughts, but they just…linger. It’s hard to focus on anything else when my mind keeps drifting back. Oddly enough, while I remember the feeling of it all quite vividly, some of the smaller details, like specific faces in the crowd, are a real blur, almost like I wasn't fully there. My wife is getting worried, says I'm not myself. This all started about two weeks after that incident, and it just hasn’t really let up.
D019-D020_h020.options:
A. Acute Stress Disorder
    B. Adjustment Disorder
    C. Posttraumatic Stress Disorder
    D. Schizoaffective Disorder (Bipolar Type)

D019-D020_h021.question: It’s been almost three weeks since the accident, and I just can't shake it. Every time I close my eyes, I see the car spinning. It’s like a movie playing on repeat in my head, completely out of nowhere, even when I'm trying to focus on the kids. Honestly, my patience is just gone. The other day, my daughter spilled her milk and I just *blew up*, shouting and blaming her, and I felt so awful afterwards. It’s not like me at all. I know this all started right after what happened, and it's making everything so difficult. I'm not sure what to do anymore.
D019-D020_h021.options:
A. Major Depressive Disorder
    B. Adjustment Disorder
    C. Acute Stress Disorder
    D. Posttraumatic Stress Disorder

D019-D020_h022.question: "Well, doc, everything just went downhill after that hailstorm last month. It wiped out a good chunk of my cornfield, and it’s been hell ever since. I find myself just staring out the window, looking at the fields, and a wave of pure dread washes over me. Even hearing the weather report on the radio makes my stomach clench. My wife says I've been a terror to be around. Just the other day, I blew up at her for asking what I wanted for dinner, shouting and cursing about how nothing matters anymore. It's like I can't control it. It’s been about three weeks now, this feeling of constant distress, but it's not like the world's ending; I'm not stuck reliving it or anything like that. I just can't seem to shake this dark cloud.”
D019-D020_h022.options:
A. Major Depressive Disorder
    B. Adjustment Disorder
    C. Acute Stress Disorder
    D. Posttraumatic Stress Disorder

D019-D020_h023.question: "It's been a rough few months, doctor. Ever since that patient's sudden allergic reaction to the anesthetic right there in my chair, everything feels… off. It’s hard to put into words, but I keep seeing it happen over and over again, like a movie playing in front of my eyes, even when I’m trying to focus on something else. Sometimes, I feel like I'm right back in that moment, the panic, the rush. And honestly, my fuses are so short these days. My husband says I snap at him for nothing. I used to be so patient, but now the slightest little thing just grates on my nerves and I just want to lash out. This all started about a month and a half ago, maybe two months after the incident happened. I know it’s not Acute Stress Disorder, because it didn’t hit me that quickly, but it’s still messing me up."
D019-D020_h023.options:
A. Major Depressive Disorder
    B. Adjustment Disorder
    C. Acute Stress Disorder
    D. Posttraumatic Stress Disorder

D019-D020_h024.question: "Honestly, doctor, I'm not sure where to start. It's been about three weeks since the company announced the merger and the subsequent layoffs, and I just can't seem to get a grip. Every time I see an email from HR or hear people talking about restructuring, I feel this intense dread, like a punch to the gut. My heart races and I can't focus. It’s hard to imagine going to work. Just yesterday, my wife was trying to talk to me about our budget, and I just... snapped. I ended up yelling and threw my coffee mug across the kitchen. The mug shattered. It's not like me; I've never reacted that way before. I'm usually so composed. I just feel constantly on edge, and these outbursts are really scaring me. I keep replaying the announcement in my head, and I can't shake this feeling of impending doom."
D019-D020_h024.options:
A. Major Depressive Disorder
    B. Adjustment Disorder
    C. Acute Stress Disorder
    D. Posttraumatic Stress Disorder

D019-D020_h025.question: "Honestly, doc, I just don't feel right. It all started about a month and a half ago. Things at the construction site got pretty rough, and a buddy of mine had a bad accident. He’s okay now, thank God, but ever since, I’ve been on edge. I find myself constantly snapping at anyone who talks to me, even for something small. My nerves are just fried, like I’m always ready to explode. Sometimes, if I hear a loud bang or even just see a safety cone, my heart starts pounding and my hands get sweaty, like I'm right back there. It’s not like those panic attacks some guys get, you know? But it's enough to mess with my head. I'm telling you, this isn't me."
D019-D020_h025.options:
A. Major Depressive Disorder
    B. Adjustment Disorder
    C. Acute Stress Disorder
    D. Posttraumatic Stress Disorder
